question.leadin: Answer the following questions related to the Seven Years' War.
question.text: The American theater of the Seven Years' War is commonly known by this name, which references the two main enemies that the British colonists fought during the war.
question.clue: Daniel de Beaujeu ("boh-ZHOH") won this war's Battle of Monongahela ("muh-non-guh-HEE-luh"), where General Braddock died trying to reach Fort Duquesne ("dyoo-KAYN").

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the early colonization of New England.
swap.text: This Puritan minister founded Rhode Island after being expelled from Massachusetts. He was one of the first abolitionists and wrote the first book about Native American languages.
swap.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

question.text: Originally intended as a fort to protect the Dutch West India Company's fur interests in the area, this settlement was handed over to the British in exchange for a tiny island near Suriname in the Treaty of Breda. This settlement was later renamed New York City.
question.clue: A fort in this settlement was constructed by what became a non-Ohio Bowling Green.

swap.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
swap.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
swap.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

question.text: This Virginia Governor's policies incited Bacon's Rebellion. This man was appointed by Charles I and replaced Sir Francis Wyatt.
question.clue: This successor to Francis Wyatt who upset his white constituency by adopting friendlier relations with Native Americans. This governor died before he could explain his actions to King Charles II.

swap.leadin: --name these things sought by New World explorers.
swap.text: A popular legend states Ponce de Leon searched for these waters that would halt his aging.
swap.clue: Juan de Solis believed this place to be located in Boinca on the Gulf of Honduras, but this may have been a mispronunciation of the island of Bimini in the Bahamas.

question.leadin: John Ingram led this rebellion after its namesake leader's death.
question.text: Name this first major rebellion in the American colonies, which was able to successfully send William Berkeley back to England.
question.clue: The leader of one side during this event attempted to ally with Cockacoeske ("ka-ka-ko-ESS-kee"), the "Queen of Pamunkey."

swap.leadin: This university's motto is Veritas, or "Truth."
swap.text: Name this oldest university in the United States, founded in the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1636.
swap.clue: Harry Starr fought the Jewish quota in this institution, which merged with all-female Radcliffe College in 1977.

question.leadin: It began following the deaths of Massasoit and Wamsutta, but more directly due to its namesake anger over John Sassamon's professed love for Jesus.
question.text: Identify this war in which the Wampanoag and Narragansett attacked New England settlements, leading to incidents like the Great Swamp Fight, whose namesake was also known as Metacom.
question.clue: A turning point in this conflict occurred with the Great Swamp Fight, after which the Narragansett were forced to withdraw.

swap.leadin: Some of the participants in this revolt were upset that Catholic priests had destroyed their kivas, or ceremonial pits.
swap.text: Identify this 1680 rebellion led by a man named Pope (po-PAY) in modern day New Mexico.
swap.clue: This conflict witnessed the death of about 900 members of the Acomans.

question.leadin: This poet states that she values the title figure's love over "whole mines of gold" in her "To My Dear and Loving Husband."
question.text: Name this poet from colonial Massachusetts who concluded that her "hope and treasure lies above" in "Some Verses Upon the Burning of our House, July 10th, 1666."

swap.leadin: Cornstalk and Blue Jacket led forces at the battle of Point Pleasant, the only major battle of this war.
swap.text: Name this conflict, led by the last colonial governor of Virginia against the Shawnee and Mingo.
swap.clue: "Cresap's War," the Yellow Creek Massacre, and the Battle of Point Pleasant were all part of Virginia's efforts against the Shawnee and Mingo in this war, which saw the resistance led by Cornstalk and Chief Logan.

question.leadin: This man sold his stock in the Royal African Company after a letter from the enslaved Job Ben Solomon changed his views on slavery and convinced him to buy Solomon's freedom.
question.text: Name this man who founded a colony intended to resettle the "unemployed and unemployable" of England which initially outlawed slavery.
question.clue: Earlier, this man led a Parliamentary committee on prison reform, which inspired him to found a haven for debtors.

swap.leadin: This politician suspended the New York legislature after it refused to recognize the Quartering Act.
swap.text: Identify this British politician whose set of namesake acts spurred the non-importation movement in the colonies.
swap.clue: A series of five acts named for this man aimed to enforce the Quartering Act in New York and to save the British East India Company. The placement of British troops in Boston due to those acts eventually led to the Boston Massacre.

question.leadin: 850 soldiers drowned in the disastrous Walker Expedition during this war.
question.text: Name this conflict, part of a larger war that saw Spanish Florida fight with the Province of Carolina and the Wabanaki Confederacy defend against New England's incursion into Acadia.
question.answerHtml: Queen Anne's War [or Third Indian War; prompt on War of the Spanish Succession; don’t read this prompt out loud!]
question.clue: During this war, British forces made three attempts, the last of which was successful, to capture the Acadian capital of Port Royal, defended by the Wabanaki Confederacy and France.

swap.leadin: This family sent Thomas Cresap north to establish a ferry in the territory of a rival colony, igniting a violent border dispute called Cresap's War.
swap.text: Name this family whose long-running dispute with the Penn family began when Charles II granted it land north of Philadelphia. This leading family of Maryland included the first Lord Baltimore.
swap.clue: Inspired by the Glorious Revolution, protestants led by John Coode led a rebellion against this family, which, in 1634, founded a British colony as a refuge for Catholics. Its leaders were called "Lord Baltimore" for short.

question.text: This colonial woman kept a copy of Bradford's books with her when she was captured during King Philip's War, which she wrote about in her 1682 bestseller The Sovereignty and Goodness of God.
question.clue: This colonial woman was captured by Native Americans during King Philip's War. Her captivity narrative includes the death of her six-year-old daughter, Sarah.

swap.leadin: Benjamin Franklin created the "Join or Die" cartoon for this meeting.
swap.text: Identify this 1754 meeting convened to discuss treaties between the Iroquois and Mohawk and the American colonies.
swap.clue: Peter Wraxall served as its chronicler, repeatedly referencing the "Fire of Friendship".

question.leadin: It's mission, as defined in an essay printed from Nov. 12-19, 1733, was to expose "the exorbitant Crimes of wicked Ministers" and to force the then-Governor, "an impudent Monster" to "receive the Lash of Satyr"
question.text: Name this newspaper, founded by Lewis Morris, James Alexander, and William Smith, Sr. as a mouthpiece for their opposition to the governorship of William Cosby and his "court party".

swap.leadin: One government passed several pieces of legislation restricting the sexual behavior of these people, such as ones "Against secrett marriage" and "Against ffornication"
swap.text: Name these people who gained rights as their behavior became more legislated through the mid-17th century. John Punch is believed to have been one of these people before losing a landmark legal case and his freedom.
swap.clue: This people who had to work for a set amount of time- usually either four, five, or seven years- in order to pay for their transport to the New World.
